Declaring roles: makes a session hold ONLY its roles' scopes, and the auto-CRUD gate checks `<table>:<action>` against them: a roles: block of capability scopes (`app:read`, MCP tool permissions) that names no table, or that omits `user` (the role every new account holds), makes every auto-CRUD call 403 `scope denied: session does not have <table>:read permission: no role the account holds grants it under roles: in app.yaml` for those accounts (a scoped API token whose own scopes leave the table out reads `scope denied: token does not have <table>:<action> permission`). Set top-level `table_scopes: access` in app.yaml to let access: rules alone decide auto-CRUD table access: the CRUD scope gate admits any schema table the role scopes don't name, a scoped API token or connector grant still narrows it, and session scopes/permissions are unchanged - so perm: modes, flow `permissions:` and MCP tool permissions keep following roles: (a table-named permission there still needs a role that grants it). `benmore check` warns when roles: would 403 every CRUD call.

`admin` is built in: a global admin (users.role = admin or a global admin grant) holds every scope when roles: does not declare `admin`, as in an app without roles:. Declaring `admin` under roles: still sets its scopes explicitly (a narrow list narrows the admin). The credential's own scopes still narrow it: an admin's API token, scoped Bearer session or connector grant reaches only what it was minted for. A tenant membership role or group-scoped grant named admin is not a global admin and gains nothing.

Unknown role names (not declared in roles:) are rejected 400 on grant, and on the admin panel's POST /_admin/set-role. `user` and `admin` always exist; an app without a roles: block has no catalogue, so both accept any name. The admin user page's role form posts to /_admin/set-role, offers user, admin and the declared roles, and says the role is global; a tenant role is set on the membership row (groups.role_field).

A tenant-scoped grant or tenant membership role (groups.role_field) named `admin` is NOT a global admin: it matches a literal `role:admin` gate on group-keyed tables in that tenant (and that tenant's own row of the tenant root) and nothing else - no admin bypass of row scoping, no other role: gate, no role: or perm: gate on a table without the groups: key, no admin console. Only _benmore_users.role = admin or a GLOBAL admin grant (group_id NULL) is a global admin. Name tenant roles for what they are (company_admin, owner) so they never look global; `benmore check` warns on the collision.

GET /api/_auth/roles (the role catalogue) and reading or changing ANOTHER user's grants need an admin with an unscoped credential; a user can still read their own assignments. The credential's own scopes decide, not the role-derived session scopes, so a roles: block that does not define `admin` does not lock the global admin out of POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/_auth/users/{id}/roles or POST /api/_auth/impersonate. A scoped API token or Bearer session is refused (403 `admin with a full-access session required`).

Lockout guard: the app always keeps one usable durable admin - an account that is not deactivated, not held at a temporary password (and verified, under auth.require_verified) and holds admin by _benmore_users.role or by a global admin grant (group_id NULL) with NO expires_at. Only such accounts count. Refused 400 (`last active admin`) for whoever asks, when it would leave none: DELETE .../roles/admin (also ?group_id=all), giving that grant an expiry by PATCH (any time, past included) or by re-granting with expires_at, and POST /_admin/set-role demoting the primary role. A time-bounded admin cannot demote the durable one either. Deactivating or unverifying that account, or deleting its row, through the admin panel (generic CRUD on _benmore_users) is refused 409; deleting or purging one's own account is refused too (see api({at:'auth'}) account_erasure). Make another account an admin with no expiry first. Operator tools (`benmore users`, delete_app_user) are not guarded: they are how an operator repairs an app with no admin. Group-scoped admin grants never count and revoking one is never guarded. POST /_admin/set-role audits every change as `role_changed` with the old and new role.
Stepping into another tenant via act-as loses roles you hold ONLY in your native tenant; global grants follow you everywhere.
Templates/hooks: {{#role "editor,reviewer"}}…{{/role}} matches any-of; {{user_roles}} (comma-separated) is available alongside {{user_role}}.

A page's `role=` gate (and its /pdf route) passes for a role held globally - the primary column or a grant with no group_id - and never for a group-scoped grant or a tenant membership role. See api({at:'frontend'}) `ssr_page_gates`.
